author_or_org: Markus Borg, Dave Hewett, Donald Graham, Noric Couderc, Emma Söderberg, Luke Church, Dave Farley

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source states that several studies have highlighted productivity improvements from AI assistants such as GitHub Copilot.
claims.quote: AI assistants like GitHub Copilot are transforming software engineering; several studies have highlighted productivity improvements.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The source states that the impact of AI assistants on code quality, especially maintainability, needs further investigation.
claims.quote: However, their impact on code quality, particularly in terms of maintainability, requires further investigation.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The planned study aims to examine how AI assistants influence software maintainability, including developers' ability to evolve code.
claims.quote: This study aims to examine the influence of AI assistants on software maintainability, specifically assessing how these tools affect the ability of developers to evolve code.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The planned experiment will use Bayesian analysis to evaluate differences in completion time, perceived productivity, code quality, and test coverage.
claims.quote: We will employ Bayesian analysis to evaluate differences in completion time, perceived productivity, code quality, and test coverage.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The study design is a two-phase controlled experiment with professional developers, where Phase 1 adds a feature to a Java project with or without an AI assistant.
claims.quote: [Method] We will conduct a two-phased controlled experiment involving professional developers. In Phase 1, developers will add a new feature to a Java project, with or without the aid of an AI assistant.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Phase 2 is a randomized controlled trial in which different developers evolve random Phase 1 projects without AI assistants.
claims.quote: Phase 2, a randomized controlled trial, will involve a different set of developers evolving random Phase 1 projects - working without AI assistants.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The source is a Stage 1 registered report accepted in principle for the 40th ICSME, not a completed results paper.
claims.quote: Accepted as In-Principal Acceptance (IPA) for a Stage 1 registration of the Registered Report Track at the 40th IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME)
